title: QBR - Veridian Systems - Health Check
summary: QBR focused on usage growth, cost per 1k tokens, a recent latency spike during peak batch windows, and roadmap alignment. Customer interested in Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, VPC/private deployment timeline, and formal security docs. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark on Dedicated pool and share detailed pricing and SOC2 docs.
next_steps: Redwood to send up-to-date pricing sheet and Dedicated sizing recommendation (Samir) - due 2026-05-06
Schedule Dedicated scoping session with infra (Leah + Marcus) - proposed 2026-05-07
Share SOC2 + security pack and KMS integration guide (Noah) - due 2026-05-05
Provision trial Dedicated pool and run benchmark (Samir & Marcus) - kickoff 2026-05-10
action_items: Samir: Send pricing + example Dedicated config (due 2026-05-06)
Leah: Prepare benchmark playbook and perf metrics to collect (due 2026-05-08)
Noah: Share security/compliance packet and KMS integration notes (due 2026-05-05)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Samir Kapoor, Leah Kim, Noah Martinez (Redwood); Rachel Turner, Marcus Lee, Priya Desai, Ethan Brooks (Veridian)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. Quick round of intros — I'm Samir, AE, with Leah our SE and Noah on CSM. Rachel, over to you for any updates before we jump in?
[00:15] Rachel: Hi all, thanks. We did a quick internal prep, main things are usage up ~35% q/q, costs creeping, and we had a latency blip last Tuesday during marketing campaign — so want to understand options. Also Priya has some security questions about KMS and audit logs.
[00:35] Leah: Great, we'll cover usage and cost, then dig into the latency incident and options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[00:45] Marcus: Quick note — our infra team is worried about cold-starts and KV cache warming, we saw spikes in p95. Some transcriptions call it K V cash in logs which is confusing.
[01:05] Leah: Right, the KV cache warm-up can cause tail latency. On Hosted we do prefix caching but for predictable loads Dedicated with prewarmed lanes helps.
[01:30] Rachel: Can you quantify the improvement? We saw p95 go from 220ms to 800ms.
[01:40] Leah: Typical delta for Dedicated for your workload profile is p95 ~200-300ms stable, whereas Hosted under bursty traffic can hit 600-900ms without prewarm. We'll share the specific numbers from similar customers.
[02:05] Priya: For security, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM options, and audit log retention—what's the current offering?
[02:20] Noah: We have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC in Console, and KMS integration — we'll send the security pack. For Private deployments we can support customer-managed keys and longer audit retention.
[02:45] Ethan: Cost question — are there levers we can tune without sacrificing quality? Quantization? Batching?
[03:00] Leah: Yes — batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles and model smaller variant routing. Redwood Optimize suggestions can recommend a batching profile that preserves p95 SLA while lowering per-token cost. We also have automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when acceptable.
[03:30] Marcus: Do you have examples for our workload (short prompts, many chat interactions)?
[03:40] Leah: For conversational workloads with mean length 120 tokens, we usually recommend a batching window of 20-30ms and KV cache retention of X (we'll provide specifics). That typically cuts cost ~18-25%.
[04:05] Rachel: About Dedicated — what's the lead time and how do we size?
[04:15] Samir: Lead time depends on pool size and region. For your scale we expect a 2-4 week provisioning timeline if we reserve capacity, shorter if you take burstable options. We'll propose a sizing with baseline and spikes.
[04:35] Priya: How about VPC / private control plane? Compliance team may push for that.
[04:45] Noah: We offer Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed network, or a VPC peering option. For highly regulated data we can do on-prem packages but that takes longer. We'll attach the matrix in the security pack.
[05:10] Marcus: Regarding the latency spike: we captured traces — seems to align with autoscaler spinning up nodes during the campaign, and some requests hit cold paths. Can Redwood instrument traces?
[05:25] Leah: Yes, Console has tracing hooks and per-route dashboards. We can add more fine-grained sampling to capture the exact code-paths. Also we can recommend autoscaler thresholds to avoid spin-up during predictable campaigns.
[05:55] Rachel: Any other cost surprises we should expect — token billing quirks?
[06:05] Samir: Billing is per-token + embeddings units. There can be differences when using streaming vs non-streaming and for cached tokens we credit less. We'll walk through the cost dashboard after the call.
[06:25] Ethan: Could you share a sample pricing sheet?
[06:30] Samir: Yes — action item to send updated pricing for Hosted and Dedicated.
[06:35] Leah: If you want to try Dedicated trial, we can provision a small pool and run a 2-week benchmark against your peak window. That will show cost delta and latency.
[06:50] Marcus: That sounds good. We'll need the benchmark playbook so we can provide realistic traffic.
[06:58] Leah: We'll prepare the playbook — goal metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency, throughput, token cost per 1k and error rate.
[07:20] Priya: On encryption, is data at rest encrypted with customer keys in Hosted?
[07:30] Noah: Hosted offers provider-managed encryption by default; for customer-managed keys we recommend Dedicated with KMS integration or Private deployment. We'll outline options in the packet.
[07:55] Rachel: Any known gaps we should be aware of?
[08:05] Leah: Nothing major; some customers ask for longer audit retention which is an add-on. Also in very low-latency use cases we tune kernels and quant profiles.
[08:30] Ethan: Roadmap questions — are there improvements planned around routing and automatic fallback?
[08:40] Samir: Roadmap includes smarter routing by cost/latency, model variant auto-fallbacks, and more Optimize recommendations. We can connect you to product PMs if you want deeper alignment.
[09:00] Rachel: Yes, interested. Also curious about unit economics projections for next quarter given growth.
[09:10] Samir: We'll model two scenarios (Hosted scale and Dedicated with reserved capacity) and show cost per active user.
[09:25] Marcus: On instrumentation, can Redwood export traces to our observability stack?
[09:32] Leah: Yes, Console supports export to common tracing backends and we have webhook hooks. We'll include config examples.
[09:50] Priya: Legal asked about data residency — do you have region controls?
[09:58] Noah: Yes, we can route requests to region-based pools; for strict residency Private is the path.
[10:10] Rachel: Let's talk about the pilot scope and success criteria. We want parity in latency (p95 < 350ms), cost <= current*0.9, zero errors during peak.
[10:25] Samir: Good. We'll design the trial to target those metrics. If Dedicated meets it, we can move to a reserved commit.
[10:40] Ethan: Timeline?
[10:45] Samir: Proposed: pricing and docs by 5/6, scoping 5/7, trial kickoff 5/10 for 2 weeks, review 5/24.
[11:00] Rachel: Sounds reasonable.
[11:05] Leah: Any concerns on our side about model compatibility or quantization?
[11:15] Marcus: We use a T5-derived conversational model, quantization sometimes introduces subtle quality regressions. Need A/B tests.
[11:30] Leah: We'll include QA checks and eval prompts to monitor semantic drift. Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts tied to eval sets.
[11:50] Priya: For audit logs, what retention options are there?
[11:58] Noah: Default 90 days; add-ons for 1 year or longer with Private deployments. We'll list pricing for extended retention.
[12:15] Rachel: Any blockers for us to start the trial?
[12:20] Samir: Need SOW approval for Dedicated trial if a reserved pool is involved, otherwise a limited trial works. We'll send a proposed SOW template.
[12:35] Marcus: We'll gather sample traffic and provide a list of critical routes.
[12:45] Leah: Also want to call out the recent incident: our ops team recommended autoscaler tweaks and prewarming to avoid cold chain — small config changes often fix this without Dedicated. We'll propose both options.
[13:05] Ethan: Could you send that recommended config snippet?
[13:10] Leah: Yes, will include as part of the benchmark playbook.
[13:25] Rachel: On the pricing, if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, what's typical discount?
[13:35] Samir: Discounts depend on size; typical range is 15-35% for annual commitments. We'll model two tiers.
[13:50] Priya: For compliance review, who will own the SSO mapping and provisioning?
[13:55] Noah: We can coordinate SAML mapping — usually customer IAM team provides attributes and we configure RBAC in Console. We'll do a joint runbook.
[14:10] Samir: Recap of next steps: Samir send pricing + SOW, Leah send benchmark playbook + recommended configs, Noah send security pack, Marcus provide traffic sample.
[14:30] Rachel: Great. Anything else?
[14:35] Ethan: One ask — can Redwood run a small A/B using a cheaper model variant to measure quality impact?
[14:45] Leah: Yes, we can route a percentage of traffic to a variant and collect eval metrics. We'll include in playbook.
[15:00] Rachel: Okay thanks, appreciate it.
[15:05] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the scoping session.
[15:15] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (K V cash -> KV cache). Links referenced: security pack (link shared after call), pricing sheet (to be shared), benchmark playbook (to follow).

End of transcript.
